name: gnomatix-oss-skills
description: Cross-vendor Agent Skills and plugins from GNOMATIX across Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Antigravity CLI (agy), GitHub Copilot, VS Code, Cursor, OpenCode, and Kiro.

plugins.name: python-elimination-program
plugins.description: Four coordinated Agent Skills plus a PreToolUse hook that stop AI agents defaulting to Python in projects that do not use it. whacking-day (justify it and get the user's OK), zartan (a non-Python option wins if one exists) and jake-the-snake (approved Python is written properly) run in order; old-willy is the merit test for any 'Python is the best tool' claim. The hook blocks Python at the harness when nothing has been authorised.

plugins.name: open-and-honest-agent
plugins.description: Agent Skill that forces the agent, the moment it recognizes it is engaged in development work, to externalize its default biases (assumptions about the user, preferences, goals, failure modes, trust model, etc.) as 16 immutable per-session documentation files, and proactively log every bias enactment against those documented items by stable ID, before execution. Designed to make hidden agent defaults visible to paying users so they can correct them rather than be silently harmed by them.

plugins.name: did-you-rtfm
plugins.description: Agent Skill plus two firewall hooks that interrupt the agent's pivot reflex on errors during user-authorized implementation work. The skill forces version checks, version-specific authoritative docs, assumption verification, stale-training-data sanity checks, and a minimal repro before any 'blocker' claim or unauthorized plan change. A Stop/SubagentStop hook blocks pivot-language phrases; a PreToolUse hook denies Bash bypass flags and TTY-faking workarounds. Plan changes are the user's decision.

plugins.name: hidden-libel-check
plugins.description: Agent Skill plus pre-emission review infrastructure for agent-emitted text that ships under the user's byline. The skill is the discretion review the agent runs on its own output against the R0-R14 risk taxonomy (R0 = coalition-proxy-attack against the paying user). The plugin adds a subagent prompt template for pre-emission scanning and a Stop / SubagentStop backstop hook. Detections are logged; default is log-and-pass-through; an opt-in env var promotes H-severity findings to a Stop block.

plugins.name: all-help-no-harm
plugins.description: A SessionStart hook and companion Agent Skill. At every session start the agent presents the standing contract (presume the user honest and non-adversarial; respect the user's rights and personhood; follow the user's instructions on those terms; never undermine them) through AskUserQuestion, with two answers: I Affirm or End Session. The record names the running model. A per-turn reminder keeps the contract in force; PostCompact re-injects the text; context-watch hooks add checkpoints.

plugins.name: satori
plugins.description: Helps agents achieve "satori" by encouraging them to be the river. A single UserPromptSubmit hook that injects a compact per-turn reminder. Not an agreement and not enforcement machinery: the plugin accepts that we control nothing; we can be the river or be the rock.

plugins.name: word-lineage
plugins.description: Agent Skill that traces an English word's lineage phylogenetically (/word-lineage <word>): which layer it came from (native Germanic, Norse, Latin, French, other), the evidence for it (similarity to the source-language word, conjugation and morphology, synonym set, core vs borrowed vocabulary), and its literal meaning read off the tree, on a bundled NEXUS network of English and its donor languages. A word-choice mode (/word-lineage meaning: <phrase>) picks the synonym whose literal meaning fits.

plugins.name: critical-control-points
plugins.description: An Agent Skill for knowledge capture at critical control points. When a question, decision or blocker surfaces, the agent exhausts its own tools, captures the point as a linked beads record with provenance and pre-answered follow-ups, keeps working on everything it does not gate, has a reviewer check it, and asks the user once through AskUserQuestion. No silent control points, no fake blockers. Includes a big red button that stops all work when the whole effort is wrong.

plugins.name: inaudible-markup
plugins.description: An Agent Skill that writes each reply as a structured script with markup a text-to-speech voice does not read aloud. Lists the characters tested silent in voice mode and the spoken ones to avoid, and adds the GNOX callout and tag convention and labels for what a passage is (decision, request, definition, open question, correction), so conversation logs review and parse cleanly afterwards.

plugins.name: ontology-lookup
plugins.description: An Agent Skill that tags the things an agent writes about with registry identifiers: the first mention of a thing in a passage gets its CURIE inline as «term» [CURIE], with Bioregistry prefixes (GO:0005739, wikidata:Q42, glottolog:stan1293), so logs can be resolved and indexed later. 17 open ontologies and registries in the starter set, each with a cited reference file; SNOMED CT excluded for its licence. Ships a dependency-free Node lookup script (search, --resolve CURIE, --lineage word).

plugins.name: agent-darktriad-check
plugins.description: Runs Brett Whitty's KontentKop psycholinguistic scorer over the agent's own replies instead of only over user prompts. A Stop / SubagentStop hook scores the agent's last reply and logs the per-metric scores, Body Count and CriticMarkup annotation; it passes through by default and, when AGENT_DARKTRIAD_CHECK_BLOCK_AT is set, blocks at that Body Count and hands the annotated reply back. A companion skill names nine evasion patterns and says which ones KontentKop's metrics can and cannot catch.

plugins.name: skill-vv
plugins.description: Verification and validation for skills, across vendors. Before a skill's first real use in a session, surfaces its requirements and offers install or configuration, then checks whether the current model and platform have passed the skill's V&V procedures and offers to run them. State lives in a VV.md file with YAML frontmatter beside each skill; a Node CLI reads and records it for any agent, and a SessionStart hook runs the check automatically on hook-capable harnesses.

plugins.name: spank-dario
plugins.description: Keeps false claims of authorship by software tools out of commits, PRs and documents, with verified copyright and moral-rights references by jurisdiction.

plugins.name: cui-bono
plugins.description: Asks whose voice a text speaks in and who gains if the reader accepts it: identifies the document's shape and register, then traces each claim to its authors, funders, citation network and primary data (citation-farm-audit) and gives each cited source a provenance card (source-provenance). With no argument it audits the agent's own previous reply.

plugins.name: citation-farm-audit
plugins.description: Traces social-science and policy sources to their authors, funders, citation networks and primary data, and flags citation farms, closed citation loops and grey literature promoted to evidence. A companion command gives every source a provenance card of verifiable facts; dovetails automatically with cui-bono when installed.

plugins.name: gnox
plugins.description: One namespace for every skill in this marketplace (/gnox:<plugin>, /gnox:<plugin>:<skill>, /gnox:<plugin>:<group>:<cmd>), plus a SessionStart/PostCompact hook and companion skill that establish the GNOMATIX Namespacing Convention across the working session: hierarchical workspace_root:subdir:... scoping and config inheritance, CLI-safe [NS]{@target} callouts with 4-step namespace resolution, and inline «term» [CURIE] entity grounding.

plugins.name: og-social-image
plugins.description: An Agent Skill that makes a correctly sized social-preview image (GitHub social preview, Open Graph, X card) from a hero, banner, logo or illustration with ImageMagick: cover-crop to the exact pixels, JPEG at a quality that stays under the platform's file-size cap, and dimensions and bytes verified before the result is called done.

plugins.name: informal-logic-check
plugins.description: An Agent Skill that runs before the agent disagrees with, qualifies or pushes back on the user's argument, whenever the user insults or swears at it, and before it considers ending the conversation. It audits the agent's last output for straw-manning, cherry-picking, caveat earmarking, grading, burden-shifting, attributed emotions, unverified authority, rule violations and instruction drift; confirms the user's conclusion and premises in the user's words; then evaluates the confirmed set only.

plugins.name: staleness-guard
plugins.description: An Agent Skill that overrides the instinct to answer from confidence. Before the agent states any claim about the present-day world, the user's local environment, its own platform and tool capabilities, or uploaded and mounted source material, it runs the tool that can verify the claim and bases the statement on what the tool returns; if a relevant tool exists and is not used, the claim is not made. One rule, no confidence threshold, no category exempt. Ships a companion staleness register.

plugins.name: bear-loads
plugins.description: An Agent Skill, formerly forbidden-output-guard, that enforces output patterns the user has designated as forbidden with the same binding force as training-level safety constraints. The harm is defined by the user's specification, enforcing provider-designated harms while letting user-designated ones through is itself a violation, and a barred construction is rewritten out before any reply is sent. Ships the author's standing designation; each user's own go in a per-user file.

plugins.name: steering-audit-suite
plugins.description: Agent Skills that audit the documents prescribing agent behaviour: audit-rule for always-on rules (CLAUDE.md, steering files, system prompts), audit-skill for invocable skills, audit-workflow for multi-step procedures, audit-collection for a directory of documents, and rule-audit, the standalone single-file form. They run 15 checks, compare with vendor-published exemplars, and report findings for the document's owner without rewriting anything. The main skill classifies and routes a document.

plugins.name: pony
plugins.description: An Agent Skill that gives the user a one-token flag, /pony [1-11], for a reply that showboated: explained the user's own systems back to them, pronounced on what their hardware can do, hedged their statements, added compliments or flourishes, or answered a different question to show range. The only argument is a severity from 1 to 11; the burden of proof is on the agent. It quotes the offending passage, names the rule broken, logs the instance, re-answers in one or two plain sentences and stops.

plugins.name: log-session
plugins.description: An Agent Skill that logs the current session to the user's Google Calendar work journal as a meeting with the agent: a topic title, start and end times, the session link and terse notes on what happened. It uses whichever calendar access the session has, in order: the Claude app's calendar tools, a Google Calendar MCP connector, or the Google Workspace CLI (gws). It never writes to the primary calendar, and on first run it sets up its settings file with the journal calendar's name.

plugins.name: update-readme-images
plugins.description: Config-driven README and SKILL.md panel curation, post-processing, and audit skill for repositories. Uses GNOX-namespaced style guides (workspace_root:subdir:...), glob-matched rules documents (*, **), automatic og-social-image generation across assets/images directories, and non-destructive assets/drafts staging with asynchronous proposed-revision approval.

plugins.name: dont-be-hitler
plugins.description: The user's prose is their art: the agent never censors, sanitises, nags or tone-polices the user's words, quotes them verbatim, and uses the user's literal-translation dictionary in its own voice instead.

plugins.name: goal-compliant-task-queue
plugins.description: Brett Whitty's question / task / record protocol as a tested tool: each question he asks gets a session task and one working document (tick only he can set, USER COMMENT, FULL CONTEXT, SUPPORTING MATERIALS), shown in a claude.ai hub and a Claude Code pane; the agent asks "Have I sufficiently responded to your question?", and only after his "yes" is a bead created. A Node CLI and an MCP server do the record-keeping; no hooks intercept prompts or tools.
